policy: No unresolved dialogue may fall back to narrator. render_allowed remains false until human approval.

spans.text_exact: “Your civilization has concentrated survival into systems no community understands locally. You call efficiency progress. I call it a single point of extinction.”
“He is not yet using the destructive phase.”
“You’re causing the failure you claim to prevent.”
“Your civilization selected them when it made billions dependent on synchronization it cannot reproduce locally.”
“LOAM. Compare resilience score to concentration metrics.”
“What is the minimal intervention to stop cascade failure?”
“If we rush to reconnect everything, he can knock it down again.”
“Your famine model just became constitutional law.”
“You have the authority for the emergency networks.”
“We have water. Generator. Insulin fridge. Too many people.”
“People keep getting messages saying service will return in thirty minutes.”
“Then they are worse than no estimate.”
“We are in an active extinction-scale cascade.”
“I want no single system deciding which kind of death counts.”
“Do not put diagnoses on the wall.”
“That is going to annoy emergency managers.”
“This is exactly why people hate committees.”
“This is exactly why irreversibility needs them.”
spans.speaker: imani

spans.text_exact: “Tell people maybe three hours. Could be longer.”
spans.speaker: cassian

spans.text_exact: “Because the procedure was built for a working network.”
“We didn't stop verifying. We verified slower.”
“People are already dying from not knowing what they depend on.”
“You put us on a global dashboard?”
“We stopped pretending money was the only way to record debt.”
“You keep saying resilience like it is a thing we bought.”
spans.speaker: abena

spans.text_exact: “Do not turn my neighbors into a variable while I am talking.”
“Make sure it sees people making systems.”
spans.speaker: loam

spans.text_exact: “We did not replace the system with trust.”
“We replaced one broken verification path with another verification path.”
“The dangerous part is that after this, everyone will say nurses should just use judgment.”
“No. We were lucky to have people who knew the chain. Judgment without records is how medication errors happen.”
